messages:
sophie: heads-up — noticed steady KV cache memory growth in long-context workloads when using INT8 keys; looks different from typical fragmentation. reproducer attached below. :thinking:
jaspreet: thanks. is this on dedicated infra or local dev? any recent kernel selection changes?
kevin: dedicated perf cluster (eu-west-2). yesterday's runtime rollback skipped a small kernel heuristic tweak that prefers fp16 kernels for short tokens; not sure that would cause growth though.
sophie: repro is here (short):
```
# run on test cluster with longctx model v2 (seq=65k)
curl -X POST https://perf-test/api/v1/infer -d '{"model":"longctx-v2","prompt":"...","seq_len":65000}'
```
logs show KV resident set drifting up ~30MB/min until eviction starts thrashing. snapshot excerpt: 
```
kv_slots_total=524288
kv_active_slots=487210
kv_frag_percent=22.7
kv_pages_int8=231456
kv_pages_bf16=148912
kv_evictions/sec=0.18 -> jumps to 12.3 after minute 7
heap_rss_mb=16384 -> 19872 over 15m
```
mike: interesting that int8 pages are higher than bf16 — suggests packing/slotization changed. can you dump slot bitmap and last-touch timestamps?
sophie: attached slot-bitmap (trimmed) and pprof output. notable: a lot of slots report last_touch far older than expected but still resident. pattern: large spans of sequential slots "pinned" by partially-complete batches.
anna: could batching heuristic be delaying completion for long requests? e.g., continuous-batching waiting for KV warmup or kernel fallback?
kevin: yes — new batching heuristic introduced `wait_for_prefill` which keeps request pinned until prefix KV warmup finishes to avoid cold misses. for longctx that can hold pages for entire request lifetime. that explains residency but not why INT8 has more pages.
jaspreet: hypothesis: INT8 packing changed slot layout (smaller per-slot payload) which increased number of pages referenced per activation because of alignment differences — compaction used to coalesce adjacent bf16 slots but int8's packing prevents coalescing, leaving interleaved slots that still map to pages. combined with `wait_for_prefill` you keep many small allocations live -> more pages, slower evictions.
kevin: makes sense. any accuracy hit observed? we usually see slight BLEU/F1 shifts with quant but not large.
sophie: yep — ran eval on a 5k QA prompt set: bf16 baseline F1=81.3, int8 with current page-coalesce AND wait_for_prefill F1=80.8 (delta -0.5). when I disabled page-coalesce and forced conservative eviction, F1 -> 80.9. so small accuracy regression correlated with packing + compaction path.
mike: could compaction be reordering keys or truncating low-order info during coalesce? we should check if compaction assumes float alignment and then loses info for int8 scale offsets.
jaspreet: action items I propose:
- add per-slot quant-scale telemetry to detect if we are applying scale-normalization during coalesce (me)
- run kernel selection trace on a subset to see if fallback kernels are forcing different KV format (kevin)
- add a short E2E eval (100 prompts) toggling `wait_for_prefill` and `page_coalesce` to measure mem growth vs F1 (sophie)
- infra job: run longctx nightly with int8 on dedicated cluster and checkpoint kv bitmap every 10m (infra-bot)

kevin: i'll start kernel trace tonight. quick thought: perhaps we should try a hybrid: allow compaction but disable scale-folding for quantized slots (cheap toggle) and see mem/accuracy.
sophie: good idea. will test hybrid. also noticed eviction queue depth stays shallow until a threshold then spikes — suggests eviction triggers are conservative and then cause IO-like thrash. lowering eviction_threshold from 85%->70% reduced spike severity in local test.
mike: ok that's actionable. can we do a quick A/B tomorrow: baseline (int8 + current coalesce), int8 + no-coalesce, int8 + hybrid-scale-safe-coalesce, and int8 + lower-evict-threshold. collect mem growth curve and eval delta.
jaspreet: assigning myself to add telemetry and a flag for scale-safe-coalesce. timeline: PR by EOD tomorrow.
anna: i've scheduled the A/B harness for 03:00 UTC; tagging infra-bot to provision extra dedicated node. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: scheduled job perf-longctx-int8-abtests at 03:00 UTC, target: eu-west-2-dedicated-pool, retention: 72h.
kevin: thanks all — keep thread updated. if anyone sees large >1% accuracy regression pause int8 rollout for that model. :eyes:
